Up to now ten HVSs are known that have Galactic rest-frame velocities exceeding the escape velocity of the Galaxy and are therefore unbound. To date only one of those, the subluminous O star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005), belongs to an old population of evolved stars.

notes: US 708: The paper cites Hirsch et al. (2005) and identifies US 708 as the only old-population star among ten known HVSs whose Galactic rest-frame velocities exceed the Galactic escape velocity; it is therefore included as a previously identified unbound star (follow-up). The paper mentions a number of SDSS sdOB HVS candidates but does not name them (T:p1-b6), so no further stars are identifiable.

US 708: The paper (Tillich, Heber & Hirsch, "Searching for Hyper-Velocity Stars") mentions US 708 only qualitatively: T:p1-b5 states "To date only one of those, the subluminous O star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005), belongs to an old population of evolved stars," and lists it among known hyper-velocity stars with Galactic rest-frame velocities exceeding the escape velocity. No numerical values (coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probabilities) are reported for US 708 anywhere in the supplied text, and there are no tables or figures. Therefore no quantities could be extracted.
